key_insight: A compact trefoil vortex knot with a Rosenhead vorticity profile can evolve in Navier–Stokes simulations to produce turbulence-like Kolmogorov energy spectra and structure-function scaling from an initially unforced flow.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a controlled numerical route for generating and studying fully developed turbulence in periodic domains, useful for benchmarking CFD methods and comparing against vortex-collision experiments.
method: Extend a compact trefoil vortex simulation to later times in a larger 4π periodic domain
Use an algebraic Rosenhead vorticity profile to improve compactness and enable finite dissipation
Analyze energy spectra, energy decay, integral-scale growth, and higher-order vorticity moments
evidence_signal: The abstract reports persistent energy spectra with Kolmogorov scaling, structure-function scaling, ν-independent finite dissipation, and decay laws E(t)∼(t+t0)^−10/7 and ℓ(t)∼(t+t0)^(2/7).
watch_item: Results depend on periodic-domain Fourier-mode treatment; excluding the largest-domain modes changes the inferred integral-scale growth rate.
paper_title: Generating Kolmogorov spectra and structure functions with a Rosenhead profile trefoil vortex knot
